Class Index

java.lang.Object
io.micronaut.runner.Index
public final class Index extends Object
The reader of MICRONAUT-INF/index.bin, the table of contents a runner jar carries so that the launcher never parses a nested archive at startup.

The index is used in place: the bytes stay in the memory mapping and every accessor is a bounds-checked read at a computed offset. Records are addressed by plain int indexes, never by objects, because materialising one object per entry would cost more than everything else the launcher does; a Micronaut application indexes on the order of fifteen thousand entries.

Validation

open(ArchiveSource, long, long) checks everything that can be checked in constant time or in time proportional to the (small) jar table: magic, format version, section bounds, a power of two hash table, a sane probe limit, and that the recorded outer file length still matches the file. Anything that would cost time proportional to the entry table, such as verifying every string reference, is checked when the record is touched instead, so that opening the index faults in only the pages it needs. Failures throw IllegalStateException carrying REBUILD_MESSAGE, because in practice they all mean the same thing: the jar was edited, truncated or rebuilt after it was packaged.

Thread safety

Every accessor is a pure function of immutable state and uses absolute ByteBuffer reads, which do not touch the buffer position, so an instance is safe for concurrent use by any number of class-loading threads. validateJar(int) writes a boolean into an array; the write is idempotent, so a race only means the check runs twice.

Since:
1.0

  • Field Details

    • REBUILD_MESSAGE

      public static final String REBUILD_MESSAGE
      The message every validation failure carries. Every corruption the reader can detect has the same cause and the same fix, so the message says what to do rather than what byte was wrong; the detail follows in parentheses for bug reports.

    • BASE_VERSION

      public static final int BASE_VERSION
      The multi-release feature version that means "base entries only". META-INF/versions/N directories start at 9, so any value below 9 selects the base entry of every chain.

    • validateJar

      public void validateJar(int jarId)
      Checks, once per jar, that the nested jar still starts where the index says it does.

      This is the second half of the staleness check: the file length caught a rebuild that changed the size, and the local file header signature catches one that did not. It costs a single four byte read the first time a jar is touched, which is why the class loader can call it before every define without measuring it. The application layer is not a nested jar and is never checked.

      Parameters:
      jarId - the jar index
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the archive no longer agrees with the index

    • find

      public int find(String logicalName)
      Looks up a logical name and returns the head of its chain.

      The chain holds every record with that name across all jars, in classpath order, with a jar's versioned aliases before its base record; resolve(int, int) picks the record that applies. The candidate's name is compared against the stored UTF-8 bytes without allocating: the lengths are compared first, then the bytes, and only a name that actually contains a non-ASCII character is decoded.

      Parameters:
      logicalName - the entry name relative to its jar, with no leading slash
      Returns:
      the first record with that name, or IndexFormat.NO_INDEX

    • findClass

      public int findClass(String binaryName)
      Looks up the resource that holds a class and returns the head of its chain.

      This is the most executed method in the launcher: every class the application loads comes through it. It never builds the resource name. The hash of binaryName.replace('.', '/') + ".class" is computed straight from the binary name, using the identity hashCode(a + b) == hashCode(a) * 31^length(b) + hashCode(b) to fold in the suffix, and the candidate is verified by comparing the stored UTF-8 bytes while mapping dots to slashes on the fly. No allocation happens on the hit path, the miss path or the collision path.

      Parameters:
      binaryName - the class name, for example org.example.Service$Inner
      Returns:
      the first record for that class, or IndexFormat.NO_INDEX

      public int next(int record)

    • resolve

      public int resolve(int chainHead, int effectiveVersion)
      Picks the record a chain resolves to for a given runtime.

      Within one jar the chain lists versioned aliases in descending version order before the base record, so the first record whose version is 0 or at most effectiveVersion is the one JarFile would return. Names under META-INF/ are never versioned, which the packager guarantees by not emitting aliases for them, so no special case is needed here.

      Parameters:
      chainHead - a record, usually the result of find(String)
      effectiveVersion - the runtime feature version, or at most BASE_VERSION for base entries only
      Returns:
      the first applicable record, or IndexFormat.NO_INDEX

    • resolveInJar

      public int resolveInJar(int chainHead, int effectiveVersion, int jarId)
      Picks the record a chain resolves to within one jar, for enumerating a resource per jar the way ClassLoader.getResources does.
      Parameters:
      chainHead - a record, usually the result of find(String)
      effectiveVersion - the runtime feature version, or at most BASE_VERSION for base entries only
      jarId - the only jar to consider
      Returns:
      the first applicable record of that jar, or IndexFormat.NO_INDEX

    • string

      public String string(int ref)
      Decodes a string from the string table.

      Reference 0 always points at the empty string the writer puts at offset zero, and means "absent"; this method returns null for it, so that a caller can hand the result straight to Package and manifest APIs, which take null for a missing attribute.

      Parameters:
      ref - a string reference, that is, a byte offset into the string table
      Returns:
      the string, or null when the reference is 0

    • validateStringReferences

      public void validateStringReferences()
      Walks every string reference in the index and checks that it lies inside the string table.

      open(ArchiveSource, long, long) deliberately does not do this: it is the one validation whose cost grows with the number of entries, and it would fault in the whole entry and string tables before the application starts. References are bounds-checked when they are dereferenced instead. Tools that dump an index, and tests, call this to check the whole file up front.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if any reference points outside the string table
